regulations.title: Business Licensing By-law
regulations.text: Every person operating a business in the City of Winnipeg shall obtain a business license from the City before commencing operations. The application must include proof of ownership or lease, business plan, and proof of insurance.

regulations.title: Business Licensing By-law
regulations.text: Food service businesses require an additional Food Service License. Applicants must pass a health inspection and maintain compliance with food safety regulations. License renewal is required annually.

regulations.title: Zoning By-law
regulations.text: Properties in Downtown Winnipeg (Zone DT1) are designated for commercial and mixed-use development. Residential units are permitted on upper floors of commercial buildings. Minimum setbacks: 0 feet from street, 15 feet from rear lot line.

regulations.title: Zoning By-law
regulations.text: Secondary suites are permitted in residential zones (R1-R4) subject to the following conditions: Maximum occupancy of 2 persons, separate entrance required, off-street parking for at least one vehicle. Application to the Zoning Officer required.

regulations.title: Building and Construction By-law
regulations.text: All new buildings must meet National Building Code standards. Construction requires a building permit issued by the City. Inspections are required at foundation, framing, rough-in, and final completion stages before occupancy permit is issued.

regulations.title: Building and Construction By-law
regulations.text: Accessibility compliance is mandatory for all public buildings and businesses. Buildings must meet AODA (Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act) standards where applicable. Minimum requirements: wheelchair accessible entrance, accessible washrooms, accessible parking spaces (1 per 25 spaces minimum).

regulations.title: Noise By-law
regulations.text: Noise levels must not exceed 55 dB during daytime hours (7 AM - 10 PM) and 45 dB during nighttime hours (10 PM - 7 AM) in residential areas. Construction work is limited to 7 AM - 6 PM Monday-Friday and 9 AM - 5 PM Saturday. No construction on Sundays and holidays.

regulations.title: Off-Street Parking By-law
regulations.text: Commercial buildings must provide minimum parking spaces based on use: 1 space per 250 sq ft for retail, 1 space per 400 sq ft for office, 1 space per 50 sq ft for restaurant. Accessible parking spaces required at 1 per 25 spaces minimum.

regulations.title: Manitoba Workplace Health and Safety Regulation
regulations.text: All employers in Manitoba must implement a workplace health and safety program. This includes hazard identification, risk assessment, worker training, and incident reporting. Workers have the right to refuse unsafe work.

regulations.title: Manitoba Employment Standards Act
regulations.text: Minimum wage in Manitoba is $15.45 per hour (as of 2024). Employees are entitled to: minimum 2 weeks vacation after 5 years, statutory holidays with pay, overtime pay at 1.5x after 40 hours per week, safe working conditions.

regulations.title: Signage By-law
regulations.text: Commercial signage must comply with the following: Maximum height 15 feet for freestanding signs, 2 sq ft per linear foot of frontage for building signs. Signs must not obstruct sightlines at intersections or block windows. Illuminated signs permitted but must not flash more than once per second.

regulations.title: Licenced Establishment By-law
regulations.text: Establishments serving alcohol require a Liquor License. Application requires: police record check, proof of responsible server training, location consent from nearby residents/businesses within 100 meters, proof of compliance with health codes.

regulations.title: Property Maintenance By-law
regulations.text: Property owners must maintain buildings in good repair including: roof in good condition, exterior walls free of damage, no accumulation of snow/ice presenting hazard, graffiti must be removed within 10 days of notice. Failure to comply can result in fines up to $500.
